_comment: Checkers that NOTHING but their own unit test ever runs (vibe-ic#381). MAY ONLY SHRINK — each entry is a checker with zero coverage of real inputs. `triage` records why an entry is still here; the wrong repair is to delete the test so the entry disappears. REMOVAL LOG: analog_corner_lib_realism_lint.py removed at v1.9.63 — vibe-ic#700 wired it into the flow, so its entry had stopped suppressing anything and had become permission. Its triage note said the checker 'refuses without its input' about `project_dir`, which every real run has; the note was standing in for 'nothing calls it', and now something does. Removed, not blanked — an entry with an empty reason is the same suppression with the reason deleted.
scope_expanded: PROG/TOOLS references must now be invocation-SHAPED (a <stem>.py filename, a real import, import_module, or a bare name held by a file that builds program filenames dynamically) instead of a bare token anywhere in the source; a checker held up only by another program's message text was previously counted as wired (vibe-ic#1347)

triage.analog_corner_margin_check.py: unwired for lack of a CALLER, not for lack of an input — it requires only project_dir, which a real run always has. Unlike the rest of that class it is unwired ON PURPOSE (vibe-ic#693), because both of its thresholds are unreachable by the producer that writes the artefact it grades. MIN_CORNERS=27 needs a voltage axis that `analog_real_corner_sweep.build_pvt_grid` does not have (3 process x 3 temp = 9, and the emitted corner dicts carry no supply field), so that rule is red on 100% of analog runs for a defect no producer can fix. And `corners[].margin` is the SPEC TOLERANCE BAND the producer copies from its target table, not an achieved margin: measured on one published artefact, nine distinct simulated values carry ONE identical `margin`, and the static default band for a common block type is 0.05 — below this gate's own 10% floor, so a TIGHTER spec makes it redder. A4's gate of record is `analog_a4_corner_sweep_check`, wired in the flow and invoked inline by the analog runner. Wireable once the producer grows a voltage axis and emits a real per-corner `margin_pct` under a key distinct from `tol`.

unwired_by_decision.checkpoint_gate_check.py: ROTTED, not merely unwired (vibe-ic#693). It runs without crashing but addresses a directory layout the flow abandoned. MEASURED over the 46 run trees on a working checkout: 46/46 FAIL at checkpoint 1, 46/46 at checkpoint 2, 46/46 at checkpoint 3 - 100 percent, and every red is path rot, not a defect. On one real DRC-clean Phase-3 run (9050 measured shapes in the layout it consumed) CP1 reports 8 MISSING of 9 because phase1_spec/01_prompt.md..05_appnote.md do not exist - the run uses phase1/generated_docs/ - and only l_layer_docs PASSes. CP2 reports 5 MISSING + 1 FAIL of 12 including two ACTIVE MIS-READS: the required-file glob for RTL resolves to the FORMAL file ([PASS] file:rtl -> phase2/stage1/formal/formal_spm.sv, a false MATCH rather than a false miss), and cell_count reports 0 cell(s) on a run that placed real cells. No insertion point exists either: grep -c checkpoint over flow/phase1_phase2_phase3.yaml is 0 - the flow has no checkpoint concept, only per-step gates. Its substance is already covered: CP1 L-doc presence by phase1_doc_presence_check (the one sub-check that passes), CP2 synth/DEF/GDS/DRC by flow steps 14/16/31/37 (gds_substance_check, drc_report_check, provenance_check), CP3 FPGA sign-off by step 37 plus the FPGA cap-gap waiver machinery. Wiring it in ANY form, blocking or reporting, is an outage that trains readers to ignore it. The repair is to rewrite the checklist against the current layout or delete the program - not to wire it. Tracked as the checkpoint-gate SKILL rot noted in skills/checkpoint-gate/SKILL.md.
